title: Real sparse execution: wall-clock of top-2-of-8 expert dispatch vs dense
follows: R1.04 (PARTIAL: sparse routing specialises at no accuracy cost)
question: Does the gather-scatter top-2-of-8 MoE MLP save real CPU wall-clock time against a dense MLP with the same total parameters, and how much dispatch overhead does it add against a dense MLP with the same active FLOPs, as the width grows (d = 64, 256, 512)?

setup.measure: median seconds per forward+backward, after 3 warm-up iterations, torch threads = all cores
variants: moe-masked (all experts computed, then masked: the naive dense execution)
setup.hardware: the container CPU (tier 0); recorded in the result

predictions.K1: at d=512, moe-gather <= 0.5x the time of dense-total (sparsity saves real time at width)
predictions.K2: at d=512, moe-gather <= 1.5x the time of dense-active (dispatch overhead bounded)
predictions.K3: at d=64, overhead dominates (reported, not gating)

prior_art: Switch Transformer 2101.03961, MegaBlocks (Gale et al. 2022, 2211.15841), Mixture-of-Depths 2404.02258
not_claimed: CPU timings on one machine; GPU kernels (Triton/Metal) are a later step (tier 1-2).
